mainTopic: Conditions and limitations in a גט: forbidden-act conditions, conditions against the תורה, re-giving a limited גט, and spoken vs. written limitations before and after the תורף.
overview: The גמרא finishes explaining how אביי reads the ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן תימא. It then brings a ברייתא that says a condition to do a forbidden act, like eating בשר חזיר, must be fulfilled before the גט works. אביי answers that this ברייתא follows the רבנן. The גמרא then asks whether such a condition should be void anyway, because it goes against the תורה. רבינא answers that it is not void, because the wife can simply refuse and stay married. Next the גמרא asks who taught the משנה's rule that the husband must take the גט back and give it again. חזקיה says it is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר, while רבי יוחנן says it can follow רבי too. Then רב ספרא and רבא argue about whether a limitation that is only spoken, before the תורף is written, ruins the גט. Finally, a ברייתא brings an argument between רבי and חכמים about written conditions, and רבי זירא begins to explain it. His explanation continues on the next amud.

steps.title: How אביי reads 'principle' and 'like this'
steps.stepSummary: According to אביי, the word 'כלל' adds the case of a condition to eat בשר חזיר, and the word 'כזה' leaves out the case of a condition to be with a certain man.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to אביי: the 'principle' comes to include pig meat; 'like this' comes to exclude 'so-and-so'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains how אביי understands two words in the ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן תימא. Just before this, it explained the same words according to רבא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי holds that a condition to do a forbidden act counts like an impossible condition, so the גט works right away. The word 'כלל' stretches the rule to cover בשר חזיר. The word 'כזה' leaves out the case of 'פלוני', because she could fulfill that one in a permitted way, so that condition does hold.

keyTerms.meaning: A general principle. Here it is the ברייתא's phrase 'this is the principle'.
To include, to bring in an extra case
To exclude, to leave a case out

steps.confusionAlert: אביי and רבא read the same two words in opposite ways. For אביי, בשר חזיר is included in the rule that the גט works immediately. For רבא, it is excluded.

phrases.english: According to Abaye, "principle"
phrases.notes: This points back to the words 'this is the principle' in the ברייתא of רבי יהודה בן תימא.

phrases.english: comes to include pig meat;
"like this" comes to exclude 'so-and-so'.
phrases.notes: He means a condition that she be with a certain man. She could do that in a permitted way, by marrying him after the divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the parallel explanation of the ברייתא's wording, this time according to אביי after it was given according to רבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For אביי, a condition to eat בשר חזיר falls under the 'principle', so the גט is valid immediately. A condition about פלוני is excluded, so it must be fulfilled first.

steps.title: A ברייתא says forbidden-act conditions must be fulfilled
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that if a husband makes the גט depend on eating בשר חזיר, eating תרומה, or drinking wine as a נזירה, the גט works only if she does it. This fits רבא but is hard for אביי.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged: 'This is your גט on condition that you eat pig meat'; if she was a non-כהן woman, 'on condition that you eat תרומה'; if she was a נזירה, 'on condition that you drink wine.' If the condition was fulfilled, it is a גט; if not, it is not a גט. This works for רבא but is hard for אביי!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks אביי with a ברייתא that treats a forbidden-act condition as a real condition that must be fulfilled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי said a forbidden-act condition is like an impossible one, so the גט should be valid right away. The ברייתא says the גט works only if the condition is fulfilled, which is exactly רבא's view. So the ברייתא seems to disprove אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: A woman who is not from a כהן family, so she may not eat תרומה
A woman who took a נזיר vow and may not drink wine

phrases.english: They raised an objection: "This is your bill of divorce
on condition that you eat pig meat";
and if she was a non-priestess,
"on condition that you eat teruma";
and if she was a nazirite,
"on condition that you drink wine";
if the condition was fulfilled, it is a bill of divorce;
and if not, it is not a bill of divorce.
According to Rava it works well; according to Abaye it is difficult!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both readings were laid out, the גמרא tests אביי's view against an outside ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's view that a condition to do a forbidden act is void and the גט works immediately.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא makes the גט depend on her fulfilling a forbidden-act condition, so the condition is clearly being treated as binding.

steps.title: אביי: this ברייתא follows the רבנן
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the ברייתא is not everyone's view. It follows the רבנן, who argue with רבי יהודה בן תימא.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי could say to you: Do you think this is everyone's opinion? Whose view is this? It is the רבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי defends himself by saying the challenging ברייתא follows a different תנא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי's ruling was only said according to רבי יהודה בן תימא, who holds that an impossible condition is void. The רבנן hold that even an impossible condition is binding. So according to them, a forbidden-act condition must also be fulfilled, and the ברייתא fits them without any problem for אביי.

keyTerms.meaning: He could say to you, meaning he would answer like this

phrases.english: Abaye could have said to you:
Do you think it is the opinion of everyone?!
Whose is this? It is the Rabbis.
phrases.notes: These are the רבנן who argue with רבי יהודה בן תימא and hold that even an impossible condition stays binding.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ אַבָּיֵי: מִי סָבְרַתְּ דִּבְרֵי הַכֹּל הִיא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the source to a different תנא (the רבנן rather than רבי יהודה בן תימא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא is everyone's view, so it contradicts אביי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא follows the רבנן, while אביי was explaining the view of רבי יהודה בן תימא.

steps.title: Shouldn't it be void as a condition against the תורה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the condition isn't void anyway, since it goes against what is written in the תורה, and such a condition is void.
steps.simpleTranslation: But derive it from the fact that he is making a condition against what is written in the תורה, and anyone who makes a condition against what is written in the תורה, his condition is void!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new challenge to the ברייתא. Even according to the רבנן, the condition should be void for a different reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leave aside whether the condition counts as impossible. Asking her to eat בשר חזיר is a condition against the תורה, and there is a known rule that such conditions are void. So the ברייתא should not have made the גט depend on the condition.

keyTerms.meaning: But derive it from (a different, simpler reason)
Making a condition against what is written in the תורה

steps.whyThisMatters: It brings in a separate, well-known rule about conditions: a condition against the תורה is void. That rule could cancel these conditions even according to the רבנן.

phrases.english: But let him derive it

phrases.aramaic: דְּמַתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא,
phrases.english: from the fact that he is stipulating against what is written in the Torah,

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל הַמַּתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה –
phrases.english: and anyone who stipulates against what is written in the Torah,
his condition is void!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְתִיפּוֹק לֵיהּ דְּמַתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the ברייתא was placed with the רבנן, the גמרא questions the ברייתא itself on a separate ground.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that a condition to eat בשר חזיר, eat תרומה, or drink wine is binding.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: These conditions go against the תורה, and a condition against the תורה is void, so the גט should work immediately.

steps.title: רב אדא: here she is the one uprooting, not him
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בריה דרב איקא says the rule 'a condition against the תורה is void' applies only when the husband himself uproots a תורה law, like שאר כסות ועונה. Here, the wife is the one who would eat בשר חזיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אדא son of רב איקא said: When we say that someone who makes a condition against what is written in the תורה has a void condition, that means a case like her food, clothing and marital rights, where he is the one uprooting the law. But here, she is the one uprooting it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 4. It explains why the condition about eating בשר חזיר is not automatically void.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that a condition against the תורה is void is limited to cases where the husband himself is breaking a תורה rule, like refusing his wife food, clothing or marital rights. In our case, the one who would break the תורה is the wife, by eating בשר חזיר. So the condition stays valid.

keyTerms.meaning: Makes a condition against what the תורה says
His condition is void (it does not count)
Her food, her clothing, and her marital rights: what a husband owes his wife

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא:
phrases.english: Rav Adda son of Rav Ika said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמְרִינַן מַתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: When we say that one who stipulates against what is written in the Torah
his condition is void,
that means a case like her food, her clothing, and her marital rights,
phrases.notes: He means a husband who sets a condition that he won't owe her these things.

phrases.english: where he is the one uprooting it;
but here, she is the one uprooting it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַדָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא: כִּי אָמְרִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4 by narrowing the rule of a condition against the תורה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the rule (only when he uproots, not she)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any condition involving a תורה violation is void.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a condition where the husband himself uproots a תורה law is void.

steps.title: רבינא: she only does it because of his condition
steps.stepSummary: רבינא objects: the wife only eats in order to fulfill the husband's condition, so in the end he is the one uprooting the תורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא challenged this: Isn't she uprooting it only to fulfill his condition? So it turns out that he is the one uprooting it!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא attacks רב אדא's answer. He says the 'she vs. he' difference doesn't hold up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wife has no reason of her own to eat בשר חזיר. She does it only because the husband made it the condition of the גט. So the real cause is the husband, and the condition should be void after all.

phrases.english: Ravina strongly objected to it:
Is she uprooting it
for any reason other than to fulfill his condition?
It turns out that he is the one uprooting it!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the distinction offered in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אדא's distinction between the husband uprooting and the wife uprooting
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Her act is only a means of fulfilling his condition, so the uprooting is really his.

steps.title: רבינא: he isn't forcing her to eat
steps.stepSummary: רבינא gives a new answer. In שאר כסות ועונה the husband definitely uproots the law. Here he does not force her to eat. She can choose not to eat and simply stay married.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבינא said: When we say a condition against the תורה is void, that means a case like her food, clothing and marital rights, where he definitely uproots the law. But here, is he telling her that she has no choice but to eat? She can not eat, and not be divorced.
steps.whatsHappening: Since רב אדא's answer fell, רבינא offers a different reason why the condition is valid.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With food, clothing and marital rights, the condition itself takes away a תורה obligation. That is a sure uprooting. Here the condition does not demand any sin. The wife can avoid the sin by giving up the divorce, so the condition does not go against the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: There is no way around it, she must

steps.confusionAlert: רבינא is not saying eating בשר חזיר is allowed. He is saying the condition is not void, because it gives her a choice: if she won't sin, there is simply no גט.
steps.whatToRemember: A condition is void as 'against the תורה' only when it surely removes a תורה rule, like שאר כסות ועונה. A condition that the other side can avoid by giving up the deal is valid.

phrases.english: Rather, Ravina said:

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אָמְרִינַן מַתְנֶה עַל מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּתּוֹרָה
phrases.english: When we say that one who stipulates against what is written in the Torah
his condition is void,
that means a case like her food, her clothing, and her marital rights,
where he definitely uproots it;
but here, is he saying to her:
"You have no choice but to eat"?!
Let her not eat, and not be divorced.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected answer of step 5 with a new answer to step 4.
steps.terutzResolutionType: New distinction: certain uprooting vs. a condition that leaves her a choice
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since only his condition makes her eat, the condition counts as his uprooting the תורה and is void.
steps.terutzMaskana: The condition does not force a sin. She may refuse and stay married, so it is not 'against the תורה'.
steps.whyThisMatters: This answers the question of step 4. A condition to do a forbidden act is not void as 'against the תורה', so the ברייתא's rule that the condition must be fulfilled can stand, following the רבנן.

steps.title: Who taught the משנה's fix: take the גט back?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: a husband who gave a גט forbidding her to one man should take it back and give it again. It asks which תנא holds this.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: What should he do? He should take it from her, and so on. Who is the תנא of this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks whose opinion it follows. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה assumes that a גט which leaves out one man is a problem that must be fixed by giving it again. The גמרא wants to know which תנא holds this, since not everyone agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: He should take it from her
Who is the תנא (author) of this?

phrases.english: What should he do?
phrases.notes: This is the משנה's case: he gave the גט but said she may not marry a certain man.

phrases.english: He should take it from her, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה goes on: he gives it again and says she may marry any man.

phrases.english: Who taught this?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד יַעֲשֶׂה – יִטְּלֶנּוּ הֵימֶנָּה וְכוּ׳: מַאן תַּנָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה after finishing the condition discussion.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which תנא holds that a גט with an exclusion must be taken back and given again

steps.title: חזקיה: it is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.stepSummary: חזקיה answers that the משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: חזקיה said: It is רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the משנה's fix follows the view of רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By naming a specific תנא, חזקיה shows that this line of the משנה is one view and not something everyone agrees to. It opens the door for the גמרא to look into what רבי שמעון בן אלעזר holds.

phrases.english: Ḥizkiyya said:
It is Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר חִזְקִיָּה: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר הִיא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

steps.title: The ברייתא showing רבי שמעון בן אלעזר's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says the husband must take the גט back, hand it over again, and say 'Here is your גט.'
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: רבי שמעון בן אלעזר says it does not work until he takes it back from her, gives it to her again, and tells her, 'Here is your גט.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up חזקיה's answer from Step 9. It shows a ברייתא where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר demands that the husband take back the גט and give it again, which is exactly what our משנה requires.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says a husband who gave a גט forbidding her to one man must take it back and give it again. The ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון בן אלעזר is the one who requires a fresh handing over in a similar situation. This is why חזקיה linked the משנה to him.

keyTerms.meaning: that he takes it back from her

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabbi Shimon ben Elazar says:
[It does not work] until he takes it back from her,
and gives it to her again,
and says to her: "Here is your bill of divorce."

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for חזקיה's claim that the משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.
steps.raayaObject: חזקיה's claim that our משנה follows רבי שמעון בן אלעזר
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון בן אלעזר requires the גט to be taken back and handed over again

steps.title: רבי יוחנן says the משנה can follow רבי too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says the משנה can follow רבי as well. Our case is different, because the limited גט already made her unfit to marry a כהן.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: You can even say the משנה follows רבי. Your own Sage said: It is different here, because she already acquired the גט in a way that makes her unfit to marry a כהן.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן gives a different answer to the question of Step 8. He says even רבי, who usually does not require a second handing over, would agree here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even a limited גט forbids a woman to a כהן, so this גט has already partly taken effect and belongs to her. Once that has happened, the husband cannot use the same handing over to finish the divorce. He must take the גט back and give it again, and even רבי agrees.

keyTerms.meaning: to become unfit to marry a כהן

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a limited גט is not just nothing. It already has a real effect, since it forbids her to a כהן.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
You can even say [it follows] Rabbi.
phrases.notes: רבי here is רבי יהודה הנשיא, who argues with רבי שמעון בן אלעזר.

phrases.english: Your own [Sage] said:
phrases.notes: He means רב כהנא, a sage from בבל who came to learn in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: It is different here,
since she already acquired it
to become unfit through it for marrying a כהן.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ תֵּימָא רַבִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to the question of Step 8, instead of חזקיה's answer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It can even follow רבי, because the limited גט already partly worked by making her unfit for a כהן, so a new handing over is needed.

steps.title: רב ספרא: the משנה speaks of a condition written inside the גט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next words of the משנה, 'he wrote it inside it,' and רב ספרא points out that the משנה speaks only of a written condition.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'He wrote it inside it': רב ספרא said: We learned 'he wrote it inside it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה. רב ספרא stresses its wording: only a condition written in the גט ruins it, not one that was only spoken.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that if the husband wrote the limiting condition inside the גט, the גט is invalid even if he erases it. רב ספרא reads this to mean that a spoken condition does not ruin the גט. The husband can then hand it over without the condition and it is valid.

keyTerms.meaning: He wrote it (the condition) inside it (the גט)

phrases.english: "He wrote it inside it":
phrases.notes: These are the words of the משנה: if he wrote the condition inside the גט, it is invalid even if erased.

phrases.english: Rav Safra said:
We learned "he wrote it inside it."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic on the next clause of the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a condition written inside the גט makes it invalid. A spoken condition does not.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רב ספרא needed to say this, since the משנה clearly says 'he wrote it.'
steps.simpleTranslation: It's obvious! We learned 'he wrote it inside it'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב ספרא: the משנה already says 'wrote,' so what did he add? This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that רב ספרא's statement seems to repeat what the משנה plainly says. The גמרא assumes a sage does not state the obvious, so his statement must be adding something.

phrases.english: It is obvious!
We learned "he wrote it inside it"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב ספרא's statement as unnecessary.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה already says the condition was written, so his point adds nothing new.

steps.title: Even before the תורף, only a written condition ruins the גט
steps.stepSummary: רב ספרא was needed because we might have thought that a condition spoken before the תורף was written would also ruin the גט. He teaches that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: What might you have said? That this applies only after the תורף, but before the תורף even a spoken condition makes it invalid. He teaches us that it does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רב ספרא added. Without him, we might have thought a spoken condition said before the main part of the גט was written also ruins it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורף is the core of the גט, with the names and the date. One might think that a condition spoken before the תורף was written shapes the whole גט and ruins it. רב ספרא teaches that only a written condition ruins it, even in that case.

keyTerms.meaning: The core part of the גט (names and date)
He teaches us (that it is not so)

steps.whatToRemember: A limiting condition ruins a גט only if it is written inside it. A condition that is only spoken does not ruin it, even if said before the תורף was written.
steps.confusionAlert: 'These words apply after the תורף' is the mistaken idea the גמרא rejects. It is not רב ספרא's final ruling.

phrases.english: What might you have said?
This applies [only] after the essential part,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the rule that only a written condition ruins the גט.

phrases.english: but before the essential part [was written],
even [a condition said] orally also makes it invalid.
He teaches us [that it does not].

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי לְאַחַר הַתּוֹרֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 by showing what רב ספרא added.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: rules out a mistaken idea
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A condition spoken before the תורף was written would also make the גט invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a condition written inside the גט makes it invalid, even when the spoken condition came before the תורף.

steps.title: רבא's view: before the essential part, even a spoken limitation ruins the גט
steps.stepSummary: רבא disagrees with רב ספרא. The משנה's demand that the limitation be written applies only after the תורף. Before the תורף, even saying it out loud makes the גט פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: The משנה only taught this (that it must be written) about a limitation made after the essential part. But before the essential part, even if it was only said out loud, the גט is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a different reading of the משנה from רב ספרא's. He says that before the תורף even a spoken limitation ruins the גט.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב ספרא said a limitation spoken before the תורף does not ruin the גט. רבא says the opposite: the משנה's 'he wrote it' only covers a limitation made after the תורף. Before the תורף, words alone are already enough to make the גט פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: The essential part of the גט, the words that actually free the woman
'They only taught this about...', a phrase that limits a teaching to one case
Out loud, spoken and not written

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two אמוראים. רב ספרא says a spoken limitation before the תורף is harmless. רבא says it ruins the גט.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
They taught this only about after the essential part,
phrases.notes: 'This' means the משנה's rule that the limitation only ruins the גט if it is written inside it.

phrases.english: but before the essential part,
even if said orally, it is also invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרָבָא אָמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְאַחַר הַתּוֹרֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view to רב ספרא's ruling in Step 14 about a spoken limitation before the תורף
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A limitation made before the תורף ruins the גט even if it is only spoken. The requirement of writing applies only after the תורף.

steps.title: רבא's instruction to the scribes shows he holds this view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that רבא is consistent. He told scribes to keep the husband completely silent until the תורף was written.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא follows his own reasoning, because רבא said to those who write גיטין: Keep the husband totally silent until you have written the essential part of the גט for him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to רבא's practical instruction to the scribes. It shows that he really believed what he said in the last step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a spoken limitation before the תורף ruins the גט, the husband must not say anything that could limit it at that stage. So רבא told the scribes to silence him until the תורף was done. After that point, words alone no longer hurt.

keyTerms.meaning: He follows his own reasoning, meaning he is consistent with what he said elsewhere
Scribes who write bills of divorce

phrases.english: And Rava follows his own line of reasoning,
for Rava said
to those who write bills of divorce:
Silence the husband completely,
phrases.notes: So he doesn't blurt out a limitation that would ruin the גט.

phrases.english: until you write for him the essential part of the bill of divorce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that רבא's ruling in Step 15 matches his practical instruction
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The husband must stay silent until the תורף is written, because anything he says before then can ruin the גט.
steps.whyThisMatters: This turns רבא's view into a practical rule for writing a גט: protect the stage before the תורף from any spoken limitation.

steps.title: A ברייתא: רבי and חכמים argue about written conditions
steps.stepSummary: רבי says every written condition ruins a גט. חכמים say a written condition ruins it only if the same thing spoken would ruin it. 'חוץ' does, 'על מנת' does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: All conditions ruin a גט. These are the words of רבי. חכמים say: Whatever ruins it when spoken ruins it when written, and whatever does not ruin it when spoken does not ruin it when written. 'Except' ruins it when spoken, so it ruins it when written. 'On condition' does not ruin it when spoken, so it does not ruin it when written.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a new argument about conditions written in a גט. It opens a new topic.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי treats every written condition as harmful to the גט. חכמים say writing changes nothing: we only ask whether the same words, said out loud, would ruin the גט. A 'חוץ' takes away part of her freedom, so it ruins the גט. An 'על מנת' is just a condition, so it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Except', a limitation that leaves out a certain man she may not marry

steps.confusionAlert: 'חוץ' and 'על מנת' are not the same. 'חוץ' cuts something out of the divorce itself. 'על מנת' leaves the divorce whole but makes it depend on something.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל הַתְּנָאִין פּוֹסְלִין בַּגֵּט, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי.
phrases.english: All conditions invalidate a bill of divorce; these are the words of Rabbi.
phrases.notes: He means conditions that are written inside the גט.

phrases.english: And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל שֶׁפּוֹסֵל עַל פֶּה פּוֹסֵל בִּכְתָב,
phrases.english: Whatever invalidates when said orally invalidates when written,

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל שֶׁאֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל עַל פֶּה אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל בִּכְתָב –
phrases.english: and whatever does not invalidate when said orally does not invalidate when written:
'Except,' which invalidates orally, invalidates in writing;

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל מְנָת״, שֶׁאֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל עַל פֶּה, אֵינוֹ פּוֹסֵל בִּכְתָב.
phrases.english: 'On condition,' which does not invalidate orally, does not invalidate in writing.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: כׇּל הַתְּנָאִין פּוֹסְלִין בַּגֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new discussion about written conditions in a גט
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי says every written condition ruins a גט. חכמים say only what would ruin it when spoken ('חוץ') ruins it when written, and 'על מנת' does not.

steps.title: רבי זירא: the argument is only about conditions written before the essential part
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא says the argument is about a condition written before the תורף. רבי makes a גזירה forbidding 'על מנת' because of 'חוץ', and the רבנן do not. He then begins to discuss a condition written after the תורף.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said: The argument is about a condition before the essential part. רבי holds that we make a decree against 'on condition' because of 'except'. The רבנן hold that we do not make a decree against 'on condition' because of 'except'. But after the essential part...
steps.whatsHappening: רבי זירא explains where the argument in the ברייתא applies and why the two sides disagree. His last words start the next point, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He limits the argument to a condition written before the תורף. רבי worries that people will mix up 'על מנת' with 'חוץ', so he decrees that even 'על מנת' ruins the גט. The רבנן don't make that decree. He is about to tell us what happens after the תורף.

keyTerms.meaning: We make a rabbinic decree, a protective rule
Because of, out of concern for

steps.confusionAlert: רבי does not think 'על מנת' is really a 'חוץ'. He only makes a protective decree so that people won't confuse the two.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַחְלוֹקֶת לִפְנֵי הַתּוֹרֶף –
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said: The dispute is about a condition before the essential part,
for Rabbi holds: We decree against 'on condition' because of 'except';

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: לָא גָּזְרִינַן ״עַל מְנָת״ אַטּוּ ״חוּץ״.
phrases.english: and the Rabbis hold: We do not decree against 'on condition' because of 'except.'
But after the essential part...

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא: מַחְלוֹקֶת לִפְנֵי הַתּוֹרֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains where the argument in the ברייתא of Step 17 applies and the reasoning behind each side
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument between רבי and the רבנן is about a condition written before the תורף. רבי decrees against 'על מנת' because of 'חוץ', and the רבנן do not.
